text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Commonwealth of Britain and its former colonies ends New York meeting with a decision to further delay imposing sanctions on Nigeria.
- Launching of newly designed Nigerian passport next year will cost around 600 million naira.
- Government demands that ministries submit certificates showing they have used funds prudently before they will be given their allocations for the fourth quarter of 1996.
- Five directors of Sterling Products may lose their seats on the board if shareholders vote in favour of the proposed merger with Smithkline Beecham.
- Coca-Cola bottler Nigerian Bottling Company is to acquire Aba-based Sapanda Soft Drinks, in eastern Nigeria, for 1.2 billion naira. Sapanda currently bottles Coca-Cola under licence from NBC.
- Maritime workers threaten showdown with the government if ports are privatised, as recommended by some experts.
